title: Incremental cushion banding & hiring model (nov 2025)
content:
Purpose: Exploratory model to test a 'cushion-banding' approach: stagger hiring and budget reserves into narrow bands that react to pricing elasticity and committed capacity. Goal is to protect runway while enabling predictable ops for Dedicated and Private customers.

High-level summary:
- Concept: Define 3 incremental cushion bands (Conservative / Operational / Growth). Each band maps to a small headcount tranche + price band triggers. Bands are filled or released based on rolling 6-week token demand and realized price elasticity by segment.
- Why: Reduces large commit bursts, aligns hiring cadence to observable price-induced demand elasticity and model mix changes.
- Primary KPIs: incremental monthly burn per band, months-of-runway preserved if higher price compression, time-to-fill per tranche, committed v. on-demand capacity delta.

Assumptions (base case):
- Starting runway (cash) = $120M
- Base monthly operating burn (ex-bands) = $5.6M (payroll, infra, S&M)
- Average fully-loaded annual salary + burden by role used below (apply monthly accruals):
  - Senior Infra Eng = $220k
  - Mid ML Eng = $170k
  - Product Manager = $160k
  - SRE = $180k
  - Solutions Eng (CS) = $150k
  - Recruiting & Ops = $130k
- Hiring fill lead-time: 8 weeks average (range 4–14)
- Preferred hiring mix for bands: 60% eng, 20% SRE/infra, 20% GTM/CS/ops
- Pricing elasticity estimate (token price -> demand): epsilon = -0.35 base (i.e., 10% price down → 3.5% demand increase), segment-weighted.
- Committed capacity discounts: Dedicated customers get 20–40% lower per-token rates depending on commit slab.

Staffing tranche table (CSV-like):
Band,Tranche size (FTE),Role mix (pct),Annual run-rate per tranche (approx),Monthly incremental burn
Conservative,6,Sr infra 2 / Mid ML 2 / Ops 2,$1,050,000,$87,500
Operational,12,Mid ML 6 / SRE 3 / Solutions 3,$2,000,000,$166,667
Growth,24,Mid ML 12 / Sr infra 4 / PM 4 / Solutions 4,$4,000,000,$333,333
Note: run-rate includes 25% benefits + equity accrual.

Pricing scenarios (three buckets):
- Scenario A (base): average price per generation token = $0.0008; elasticity -0.35; net revenue retention stable
- Scenario B (compression): price down 15% vs base (market pressure); elasticity -0.5 for low-commit segments → topline decline for on-demand-heavy customers
- Scenario C (price expansion): price up 10% because of better unit economics and new premium feature; elasticity -0.2 (demand softens modestly)

Model outputs (illustrative):
Table (pricing scenario -> burn delta -> runway impact if bands fully hired):
Scenario,Extra monthly infra cost (tokens),Revenue delta (monthly),Net monthly burn delta,Runway months delta (from base 21.4 months)
A (base),$220,000,$0,$220,000,-0.9
B (compression),$320,000,-$550,000,$-230,000,+1.1
C (expansion),$180,000,+$420,000,$-240,000,+1.2
Interpretation: under compression the platform may see net negative revenue delta (reduced take) but lower price can drive slightly higher demand; net effect is scenario dependent. The banding reduces downside because we can avoid filling Growth band until trend confirmed.

Band activation rules (draft):
- Conservative band: always filled (safety ops) — incremental burn booked as fixed cost.
- Operational band: triggered when 6-week trailing committed capacity utilization > 70% and price realization within 5% of base.
- Growth band: only filled when 12-week trend shows >8% sequential token volume growth OR new enterprise commit pipeline > $3M ARR.
- Decommissioning: if 6-week trailing demand drops >12% and price compression below trigger, freeze hires and redeploy FT budget into on-call contractors for up to 16 weeks.

Pricing sensitivity sweep (notes on approach):
- We run a matrix sweep across price multipliers [0.85, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1] and elasticity assumptions [-0.2, -0.35, -0.5].
- For each cell we simulate monthly token volume, revenue, infra cost delta, and required committed capacity (GPU-hours).
- Output metric: "breakeven band fill" — the probability that filling Operational+Growth within 12 weeks is net accretive to gross margin given scenario.

Example cell (price 0.9, elasticity -0.5):
- Expected token volume change: +5% (0.9 = 10% price drop; delta volume = 10% * 0.5 = 5%)
- Revenue change: -5% revenue vs base (price * volume effect combined) → net revenue decline = -5%
- If on-demand infra cost grows faster than price decline (because of cache miss rates), gross margin compresses and we recommend holding Growth band.

Sensitivity outputs (quick shortlist):
- High elasticity (-0.5) + price cuts: modest volume gains do not fully offset revenue loss; avoid filling Growth band unless committed discounts are locked.
- Low elasticity (-0.2): price increases can lift revenue quickly and justify partial Growth band fills; time-to-fill remains gating factor.
- Recruiting lag amplifies downside: 8-week fill means band decisions are always reactive — we model 2-week earlier signal requirement for Growth.

Risk register (brief):
- Market shock: sudden 30% price compression in open market reduces take rate and increases churn risk. Mitigation: hold Growth hires, accelerate enterprise commit campaigns.
- Hiring mismatch: can't reprioritize openings quickly -> use contractor pool (estimated cost premium +30%) for short-term scaling.
- Forecast bias: elasticity estimates may be off by ±0.2. Run weekly posterior updates with product telemetry.

Action items (owner tags):
- Priya: finalize a 12-week dashboard for band signals (connect usage, price realization, commit pipeline) — due 2025-11-21.
- Ethan: wire the pricing sweep outputs into the finance forecast model and add scenario toggles — due 2025-11-14.
- Marta: validate recruiting lead times by role and propose a contractor bench budget — due 2025-11-28.
- Samir: run sensitivity on committed discount acceptance rates (simulate 10/20/40% take) and produce recommendation for Dedicated slab pricing — due 2025-12-05.

Appendix (quick formulas):
- Monthly incremental salary = (annual salary * (1 + benefits_rate)) / 12
- Revenue change approx = price_change + price_change * elasticity (small-change linearization)
- Runway months = available_cash / (base_burn + sum(band_burns) - net_revenue_delta)

Notes / open questions:
- Do we want an explicit "reserve bucket" (cash set-aside) for one-off infra scaling (GPUs) tied to Growth band? If yes, recommend 3x monthly incremental infra cost for Growth as a buffer.
- Should we include customer-level sensitivity (enterprise vs PLG) in the default band triggers? (likely yes; propose adding segment weights).

Version history: initial draft 2025-11-07; scenario updates 2025-11-21; sensitivity re-run 2025-12-12; current in-review 2026-01-15.
